jess: Heads-up — Client Gamma (Dedicated pool) asked for stricter per-request token budgets and lower queue depth. They reported P99 spikes after we tweaked kernel selection. Can we draft a safe batching config for them that avoids regressions? I attached profiler link: https://internal.prof/gamma/175321.

mike: Can you paste the profiler highlights here? Are we seeing KV cache thrash or just oversized batches?

jess: Quick summary from profiler: 
- P95 token latency spikes when effective batch size > 8 on seqlen ~1024.
- KV cache miss rate increases ~12% after ~10k requests (prefix diversity).
- Kernel selector often picks 16-bit matmul path for short sequences but on Gamma's GPU that path has poorer latency due to small warp utilization; we fall back to float32 kernels sporadically causing memcpy overhead.
Link to perf traces: https://internal.traces/gamma/trace-175321.

perf-alert-bot: [alert] Regression detected in pool "dedicated-gamma": +18% p99 generation latency since last rollout. See /alerts/175321.

sophia: Thanks. My initial thought: give them conservative defaults so we don't thrash KV and keep p99 stable. Proposal: token_budget_per_request 1024, max_queue_depth 150, batching_window_ms 12. Pin hot prefixes for 5m to reduce cache churn.

oliver: Agree on conservative. Also recommend a dynamic token budget: start with min(1024, user_req_tokens) but shrink batches for high prefix-entropy paths. We can expose a per-customer override so support can tighten.

mike: Would like to validate with a short A/B on their pool. Run these steps:
1) collect kernel selection stats: `observe_kernels --pool dedicated-gamma --model xglm-13b --seq-len 1024 --duration 120`
2) run micro-batching profile: `tools/run_profiler --pool dedicated-gamma --duration 60 --output /tmp/gamma.prof`
3) simulate prefix diversity with loader: `python scripts/sim_prefixes.py --qps 200 --prefix-entropy high`

jess: If we go this route, here's a config snippet I propose we push as a canary:```json
{
  "token_budget_per_request": 1024,
  "max_queue_depth": 150,
  "batching_window_ms": 12,
  "batch_max_items": 8,
  "kv_cache_pin_ttl_s": 300,
  "dynamic_shrink_threshold": 0.25
}
```

oliver: Two notes: set `batch_max_items` to 8 matches the plateau observed. `dynamic_shrink_threshold` means if observed increase in miss-rate > 25% we reduce batch window by 50%. Also suggest kernel-hinting flag for this customer: `prefer_fp32_short_seq=true` to avoid fallback overhead.

sophia: Good. Can we add a metric-based rollback: if p99 increases > 10% vs baseline for 10m, auto-roll back to previous config?

mike: Yes. We'll wire a canary with a 10-min evaluation window and early rollback. I can run the profiler steps tomorrow and post raw traces.

jess: OK, I'll draft the config request for infra (customer-specific overrides + canary policy). Tagging @eng-runtime for visibility. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
